## Intent

The bug is real at a configuration nobody runs. Post-mortem addition: it catches findings that are mechanically correct and unreachable under the deployed parameters.

## Detection signals

Signals describe the mismatch between the analysis and the deployment: "at the documented configuration", "assuming a non-default config", "if the operator chooses".

Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the full text of the
draft finding, subject to the engine rules below.

**Fires when at least one of these matches:**

```text
  at the documented (configuration|stablecoin|setting)
  no misconfiguration
  not how (it|the protocol) is (run|deployed|configured)
  assuming (the |a )?(non[- ]standard|unusual|non[- ]default) config
  if the (operator|maker|admin) (chooses|sets|ships)
  under the deployed configuration
```

## Escape hatches

None. The fix is to name a bound that is representative of the deployed configuration, and that is a change to the analysis rather than to the phrasing.

## Known false-positive modes

These are the shapes where the rule fires on something it should not. They are the
reason a firing is a prompt to check, not a verdict.

- A finding measured at a representative deployed bound that also mentions a non-default configuration in a sensitivity note.
- A program whose deployed configuration is genuinely operator-set, so no single "documented" configuration exists.
- A report about a parameter that is immutable in the deployed bytecode but configurable in the source.

## Synthetic examples

Both examples are synthetic. They describe no real report and no real target.

**Fires:** "At the documented configuration the margin is negative, so assume a non-default config where it is positive."

**Does not fire:** "Measured at the deployed configuration with representative bounds."

## Corrective action

Name at least one bound representative of the deployed configuration. If no bound is representative, the headline cannot set severity.
